title: Bare `resume` becomes a usage error (backwards-incompatible)
body: Previously, `jarvis resume <plan>` clears every plan-declared gate + active breakers + active defers in one shot. After this plan: bare `resume <plan>` exits 2 with a usage message; the bulk-clear behavior moves behind `--all`. This is backwards-incompatible — any operator script or muscle-memory invocation of bare `resume` will break. Why: (a) the bypass discovered during the patch-completeness F001 dogfood proved the current default is dangerous in practice, not just in theory; (b) the population of bare-`resume` users is small (just dogfood operators) and the breakage is loud (exit 2 with a clear remediation message), so the migration cost is low; (c) safe-by-default is the right invariant for any command that mutates gate state. How to apply: future CLI commands that mutate platform state should default to safe-by-default (exit 2 with usage on missing flag) rather than 'do the most destructive thing on bare invocation'.

title: Auto-continue after gate clearance is deferred
body: Considered: when `approve <gate>` or `resume --gate <name>` clears the last unmet gate AND a paused volley exists in the active_supervisors registry, automatically re-dispatch the volley. Rejected for v1. Why: (a) the operator may have other state to verify (quota readiness, target_context correctness) before re-dispatch — auto-continue would skip the second human checkpoint that the gate was meant to provide in the first place; (b) the current pattern (re-run `dispatch-from-plan --confirm`) is one extra command but keeps the operator in the loop; (c) auto-continue is more magical than explicit, and explicit is what the platform optimizes for elsewhere (see D004 of the security-baseline plan, D002 of the patch-completeness plan). How to apply: if a future need to reduce the friction surfaces, prefer printing a `next: <command>` hint after the last gate clears rather than auto-running the dispatch.

title: Renaming `resume` is deferred
body: The verb 'resume' suggests 'continue execution,' but the platform's `resume` is actually 'clear gates' (and the volley does NOT continue automatically — the operator must re-dispatch). This semantic mismatch contributed to the originating finding: assistant typed `resume` after `approve` expecting it to mean 'continue,' got 'clear all remaining gates' instead. A rename (e.g. `resume` → `clear-gates`) would fix the semantics but has wider blast radius (every doc reference, every operator's muscle memory, the F008 + F006 + F007 plan-evidence trail). Deferred to a future plan that owns the rename + migration + doc sweep. Why: this plan is small and surgical; bundling the rename would push it into a multi-week change. How to apply: when the rename plan is opened, cite this D-entry + the originating-finding evidence as the motivation.

title: Originating finding cited as evidence; plan 2026-05-01-004 left in current gate state
body: The triggering finding occurred during dogfood of plan 2026-05-01-004 patch-completeness F001. The dogfood is paused — gate-state.json shows pre_impl + pre_merge cleared via the buggy bare-`resume`, but no audit envelopes were written (the resume command doesn't itself dispatch). The plan's gate state is preserved as-is for evidence; this resume-discipline plan ships the fix. Why: rolling back plan 004's gate-state.json now would erase the evidence we're using to motivate this plan. How to apply: see D005 for the corrected recovery framing — re-arming pre_merge does NOT restore post-implementation review protection because the supervisor evaluates all human_gates upfront.

title: F001 close-out — 3 of 4 findings resolved manually; 1 deferred to plan 005 with audit-trail integrity preserved
body: F001 ships passes:true after a volley → manual-fix → confirmation-volley arc. Audit history (8 envelopes from 2 volleys) preserved verbatim — no envelope JSON was edited post-hoc. Resolution map: (1) medium event-body parity finding from initial volley → resolved by normalizing approve/resume INBOX bodies + adding strict equality-modulo-entry-phrase test; (2) low stale-docstring finding from initial volley → resolved by updating gate_pause.py + circuit_breakers.py module docstrings; (3) low parametrize finding from confirmation volley → resolved by refactoring 7 separate test functions into one @pytest.mark.parametrize driver dispatching to per-shape handlers; (4) high command-accountability finding from confirmation volley → DEFERRED. The HIGH finding is `target_context.commands_run: []` because the implementer formatted side-effect commands as bullet+backtick rather than the literal `^$ ` line-start format the supervisor's prose-extraction regex expects. This is platform-formatting debt, not feature behavior — it is the exact EC5-class issue plan 2026-05-01-005-feat-target-context-platform-fix exists to solve at the platform layer (write-side prelude injection + auditor severity downgrade with description preservation per that plan's D008). Why defer rather than fix here: editing the audit envelope post-hoc would fake the audit trail and destroy the very evidence motivating plan 005; re-volleying produced different findings each round (stopped_no_progress → stopped_diminishing_returns), suggesting the loop is now measuring platform-shape limits more than feature defects. How to apply: see evidence/closeout-memo.md for the full resolution table + volley-instability observation. F001 is feature-complete; the deferred finding's owner is plan 005.

title: Current platform truth: human_gates are upfront admission gates, not sequential checkpoints
body: Discovered during this plan's own dogfood: the supervisor evaluates ALL declared `human_gates` BEFORE the implementer runs. Approving one and leaving another armed causes immediate re-pause without dispatching anything. So `pre_merge` is functionally an upfront admission gate (a second 'are you sure?' before the volley begins), NOT a sequential checkpoint that fires post-implementer-pre-signoff. The 'two-checkpoint protection' intent operators have been reaching for does not exist in the current platform. This contradicts the natural-language reading of `pre_merge` and is the same gate-model gap surfaced in the 2026-04-29 dogfood lessons memory. Implications: (a) every prior signed-off plan that declared `pre_merge` actually had the operator approve it upfront, with signoff review happening after-the-fact via gate-state-history reading and INBOX inspection, NOT via a sequential pause; (b) plan 2026-05-01-004's recovery (D004 above) cannot 'restore' post-impl review protection by re-arming pre_merge — re-arming only adds another upfront pause; (c) honest recovery for plan 004 is operator-choice between accepting the cleared state (with this D-entry as the audit reason) OR re-arming pre_merge as an explicit upfront checkpoint, both of which produce equivalent post-volley review semantics. Why: discovered while dogfooding this plan; documenting in audit history is more honest than letting the misleading `pre_merge` semantic propagate. How to apply: **queued (not opened)** — a future platform plan should either (a) implement phase-aware gates (`pre_impl`, `pre_signoff`, `pre_merge` each firing at distinct lifecycle points) OR (b) rename/remove misleading gate names from templates so operators stop reaching for protection that doesn't exist. Until that plan lands, treat `pre_merge` as 'extra upfront confirmation' and rely on post-volley review of audit envelopes for findings discipline.

title: Status-flip close-out — active → completed; gate-Q verified live, three-layer Q2 classification recorded
body:
Tier 2/3 fifth close-out (after warmup 5a0979b + validator-dispatch 03cc0b9 + EC5-purity 271870c + onboarding-ux e6ffa32). D006 already recorded the impl-time close-out (3 of 4 findings resolved manually, 1 deferred to plan 005); this entry records the formal status-flip and the cross-plan + Q2-classification + gate-specific-Q verification that did not exist when D006 was written.

Eight-step + Q1/Q2 + gate-specific Q executed. (1) `git ls-tree HEAD --` showed 16 tracked / 14 worktree → 2 tracked-MISSING files (`audit/codex-auditor-i1.json` + `evidence/finding/originating-gate-state.json`). Restored from HEAD via `git checkout HEAD --` — partial-clone fallout, same shape as Plan 2026-05-02-003's missing decisions.jsonl earlier in this session. Bidirectional ls-tree check caught it precisely. (2) Validator clean before flip; full re-validate after restore exits 0 across plan.md, features.json, 4 audit envelopes (i0/i1 implementer + auditor), signoff JSON; auxiliary gate-state.json visibly skipped. (3) F001 passes:true; D001-D006 with schema {id, ts, by, title, body} (D005 placed after D006 in file — non-monotonic but complete set). Q1: 2 closed-plan citers in Plan 2026-05-05-001 (mechanical fixture-path enumeration in D008 + plan.md) + 2 ACTIVE citers in Plan 2026-05-01-005 (the deferred HIGH finding's target — bidirectional dependency, NOT a supersession risk for this close-out). Q2 (three-layer terminal): Layer 1 = initial volley `stopped_no_progress` = platform artifact (verdict-based check_no_progress, separate from the count-based fix); Layer 2 = confirmation volley `stopped_diminishing_returns [2, 2]` = platform artifact since fixed (Plan 2026-05-02-004 reclassifies); Layer 3 = F001 implementation = clean (9 dispatch tests, 342/6 sweep, ruff/sanitization clean, 11 ACs verified via Path 1 manual remediation); Layer 4 = deferred HIGH finding (commands_run formatting) = META platform-formatting debt owned by Plan 2026-05-01-005, structurally resolved by plan 005's F002+F003 (audit_writer prelude injection + EC5 severity classifier downgrade), with plan 005's own status flip pending in the close-out queue.

Gate-specific Q (operator-named): does plan preserve distinction between specific-gate / bulk-clear / breaker bypass? VERIFIED YES via live `dontpanic resume --help` + bare-resume exit-code test + cli.py:203-215 inspection. Three explicit modes: (a) `dontpanic resume <plan> --gate <name>` clears one specific declared gate (parity with `dontpanic approve <plan> <gate>`); (b) `dontpanic resume <plan> --gate breaker:<kind>` clears one specific breaker (named bypass — `breaker:<kind>` strings are valid `--gate` targets); (c) `dontpanic resume <plan> --all` is the explicit bulk-clear of every plan-declared gate + active_breakers + active_defers (legacy behavior, now behind required flag); bare `resume <plan>` exits 2 with usage block (verified live: stderr usage, $? = 2). INBOX `gate_hit` template + `--help` epilog both name `approve <gate>` as preferred for partial clearance. **No silent-bypass path exists** — every clearance operation requires a named flag and emits a structured INBOX event.

(4) Plan-level memo amendment: existing `evidence/closeout-memo.md` content NOT modified. Appended single new section `Status-flip close-out verification (added 2026-05-07)` with: gate-Q verification table (4 explicit modes), Q2 four-layer terminal classification, deferred-HIGH-finding disposition (Plan 005 implementation-complete but status-flip pending), brand-rename drift note (jarvis → dontpanic in CLI form, AC behavior identical), explicit non-subsumption list (verdict-based no_progress hardening / auto-continue D002 / rename D003 / Plan 005's deferral / audit-envelope filename collision via Plan 002 all stay separate).

(5) D007 appended without reconstructing D001-D006 — single-line append after sequence-integrity guard verifying the D001..D006 SET is intact (file order is non-monotonic D001/D002/D003/D004/D006/D005, schema doesn't require monotonic ordering). (6) `dontpanic plan close` exempt-flow path (goal_type=None). (7) Re-validate clean post-flip. (8) Commit scoped to plan dir; commits exactly 3 files (decisions.jsonl + plan.md + appended evidence/closeout-memo.md).

Reason: fifth Tier 2/3 close-out, gate-discipline plan with substantial real-world dogfood backstory. Closing it makes the operator-acceptable resume CLI gate discipline visible as a closed deliverable rather than implementation-complete-but-active. The CLI behavior verification this turn confirms current state matches the locked acceptance under post-canonical-module-rename invocation form (`dontpanic` instead of `jarvis`).

How to apply: future plans depending on resume CLI gate discipline can rely on the locked safe-by-default behavior. Operators should expect bare `resume` to error, not silently bulk-clear. Verdict-based `stopped_no_progress` hardening + auto-continue + rename remain queued — do not retroactively claim coverage by this plan.

Narrative coherence (5-for-5 in Tier 2/3): warmup 2026-05-02-004 closed cross-plan stopped pattern; 2026-05-05-001 closed auxiliary-skip narrative; 2026-05-04-004 closed Phase B EC5-purity; 2026-05-01-001 reclassified onboarding volley terminal; this plan closes the resume gate discipline + reclassifies its own confirmation-volley terminal via the now-closed signature-based breaker.
